why_this.title: Why this exists
paragraphs: The freedom of any society depends, more than on anything else, on how well informed it is.

Sredstva is an independent publication by Aning Film d.o.o. and is not an official HAVC site. The registry is built exclusively from documents that the Croatian Audiovisual Centre (HAVC; hereafter: the Centre) has published: tabular results of public calls, jury narratives and individual decisions. Every amount in the registry leads to its source document. Sredstva complements the Centre's official publication; it does not judge it.

The Centre publishes its decisions regularly and publicly; Sredstva adds no new information to them, only a form. The decisions are issued as PDF documents, so they cannot be searched across years, filtered consistently or totalled reliably. Publishing public information in a machine-readable, open form as well is the direction promoted by the Croatian Act on the Right of Access to Information (re-use of information) and Directive (EU) 2019/1024; Sredstva offers that form today, built from the existing official publications and without any additional work for the Centre.

Croatia has open-data portals at the national ([data.gov.hr](https://data.gov.hr)) and local ([data.zagreb.hr](https://data.zagreb.hr)) level. This registry shows what a dataset on public funding of audiovisual activities could look like on such a portal: one record per award, with project, recipient, authors, programme, round, year, amount and a link to the source.

The registry was developed with Aning Film's own resources in 2026. It has been public since May 2026 (public repository and full dataset since 17 May). By the end of August four dated editions had been published: May, June, July and August. As of 31 August 2026 the registry holds 1,021 documents, 9,561 records and 6,593 groups of linked projects for the period 2008–2026. How it came together, step by step, is described on the [Process](#/process) tab.

The initial extraction of data from the published documents combined deterministic scripts with a machine-reading model for documents. That approach speeds up the work but does not guarantee accuracy; that is why the registry is published with a publicly marked verification status for every record, the original value is never deleted, and every amount carries a link to its source document. For anything with consequences, check the source PDF.

The application is served on the Cloudflare Workers platform. It boots from a slim 5 MiB projection of the registry (under 1 MB over the wire, compressed), while the full 18 MiB database remains published unchanged as the source of truth ([data.json](https://havc.matijar.info/havc/data.json)). The code is plain HTML, JavaScript and CSS with no third-party dependencies. FontAwesome icons and Google Fonts are used for presentation; nothing stops working without them.

The code is released under the EUPL 1.2 licence; the schema, documentation and the independently created structured data under CC BY 4.0. The texts of the Centre's source documents are reproduced in the dataset solely for verification, always with a link to the source; the rights to them remain with the Centre. The registry contains only personal data that the Centre has already published in its decisions (names of applicants and authors next to a project and an amount) and does not combine them with other sources.
The code and the full history of its development and changes are public: [github.com/matijarma/havc-explorer](https://github.com/matijarma/havc-explorer).

who_i_am.title: Who I am
paragraphs: I am the author and editor of the Sredstva registry: concept, data model, four editions in 2026 and the public code. With the Centre's support I took part in the EAVE European Producers Workshop 2014, the EAVE Film Finance Forum 2012, AdaptLab 2012 (TorinoFilmLab), BDC Discoveries 2014 and the Media Business School 2013. I am the director and co-writer of the experimental film Violinist (Studio Kubus, Centre support 2010), the author and director of the projects Jabuka and Odbjegli Twingo (Centre development support, 2014) and the head of the complementary-activities programme Croatia goes cross media (Centre support 2013 and 2014). Aning Film d.o.o. (Aning usluge d.o.o. in sources up to 2014) is the minority co-producer of the film Život kao novčić (2013). The grants in brackets can be verified in this registry.

I have been studying art and computing from about as early as a person can. It started before primary school, and not long after came the drama studio of the Zagreb Youth Theatre, where I grew up and spent my formative years. A love of drama and screen acting turned into something else once I came of age and failed the acting entrance exam at Zagreb's Academy of Dramatic Art: first into film directing, then into creative producing.

While all that growing up was happening on stage and in Zagreb's cinemas, I was also following every hertz and every byte of every electronic device I was allowed to touch. Devouring books, films and plays with one hand and taking apart every piece of software and hardware within reach with the other, I settled on drama and computing as the two fields I would work in and draw from. That is why I treat computing not merely as a tool, but as a means of standardisation and transparency and a guarantee of the efficient systems that the fragile budgets of independent art depend on.

This registry is the simplest possible demonstration of that approach: data that has always been publicly available on the Centre's official website, arranged in a form in which it can be searched, compared and re-used.
Corrections, additions and questions are welcome at [info@umjetnostzasve.hr](mailto:info@umjetnostzasve.hr). Every correction is recorded in the repository's public change history.
